atoms.b:
The First British Empire began in ((the_16th_century)).
The Second British Empire lasted from roughly ((1815)) to ((1945)).

b: British colonialism is characterised by its peaceful nature.

atoms.b: The main goal is the exploitation of the colonised land and people.
The main characteristic is large-scale European settlement.
The main goal is to integrate into local communities.

instruction.text: What could count as resistance against colonialism?

atoms.a: At its height, the British Empire was the largest colonial empire.
The British Empire mainly consisted of settler colonies.

feedback.wrong: The British Empire consisted of both settler and extractive colonies.

atoms.a: The very first independent British colony was India.

feedback.wrong: The first independent colonies were Canada, Australia and New Zealand. India was only the first extractive colony to gain independence.

atoms.a: Colonialism helped colonised people by introducing industrial innovations.

feedback.wrong: This is a colonial narrative and not strictly true. While colonisation changed the pre-colonial cultures, the violence and wealth extraction hurt many people and has lasting negative effects.

atoms.a: Many former colonies were forced to join the Commonwealth of Nations.

feedback.wrong: Many former colonies voluntarily joined the Commonwealth of Nations.

atoms.a: Humans cannot be separated into different biological races.
Resistance can appear in different forms.
British political and economic power were only made possible because of colonialism.
